questions.question: A churn score is consumed by a campaign that runs once each morning. Which serving pattern is the best starting point?
options: Request-time online inference for every page view
Scheduled batch scoring before the campaign runs
A stateful stream processor with second-level windows
Online learning after every customer event
questions.explanation: Batch scoring is simpler and efficient when predictions can be prepared within the product's freshness window.

questions.question: Why must a deployed model be linked to a feature version?
options: To make the feature store choose a larger machine
To avoid collecting outcome data
To ensure serving inputs keep the meaning the model was evaluated with
To guarantee the model is unbiased
questions.explanation: A model is valid only for the feature semantics, units, defaults, and time boundaries used in its evaluation.

questions.question: A shadow deployment is useful because it does what?
options: Runs the candidate on production inputs without giving it decision authority
Retrains the candidate from live labels on every request
Deletes the current model after an offline test passes
Guarantees that online business metrics will improve
questions.explanation: Shadow traffic exposes feature, latency, output, and capacity behavior while keeping users on the current policy.

questions.question: Feature freshness is healthy, but p99 inference latency and fallback use both rise during a traffic burst. What should the first response target?
options: Label taxonomy
Serving saturation and containment
A longer training history
A different offline accuracy metric
questions.explanation: The evidence points to a serving-path capacity incident, so the immediate goal is to contain user impact and restore the SLO.

questions.question: Why should prediction logs include exposure or action identifiers before outcomes are used for retraining?
options: The current policy influences which examples and outcomes are observed
Exposure identifiers eliminate every source of confounding
They replace feature and model versions
They make delayed labels arrive immediately
questions.explanation: Observed outcomes depend on what the system showed or selected; without exposure context, feedback can encode policy-driven selection bias.

questions.question: Which set of evidence is sufficient to promote a candidate safely?
options: A higher aggregate offline score by itself
A successful training job and a newer framework version
Offline slice and robustness checks, production-path evidence, canary guardrails, and a rollback path
Lower model latency without any outcome measurement
questions.explanation: Promotion needs model, system, safety, and product evidence plus a way to limit and reverse exposure.
